    Compute Gaussian Process Log-Likelihood (with Optional Quadratic Mean)

    compute_like.Rd

    Evaluate the (negative) log-likelihood of observed data under a Gaussian Process model, optionally including a linear-plus-quadratic mean function.

    compute_like(
  length_scale,
  x,
  y,
  signal_var,
  noise_var,
  D,
  quad = FALSE,
  nu = Inf
)

    Arguments

    length_scale

    Positive numeric scalar or vector of length-scales for each dimension.

    x

    Numeric vector or matrix of training inputs (rows = observations).

    y

    Numeric vector of training responses.

    signal_var

    Positive numeric scalar specifying the GP signal variance (\(\sigma^2\)).

    noise_var

    Positive numeric scalar specifying observation noise variance.

    D

    Integer. Dimensionality of the input space (number of columns in x).

    quad

    Logical; if FALSE (default), assume zero-mean GP. If TRUE, include a mean function \(_0 + x^ _1 + (x x)^ _2\).

    nu

    Positive numeric specifying the smoothness parameter for the Matérn kernel. Defaults to Inf, selecting the Squared Exponential kernel.

    Value

    A numeric scalar giving the negative log-likelihood (up to an additive constant). Extremely large values (\(>1e20\)) are returned if the computation produces NaN, NA, or infinite results.

    Details

    **Zero-mean GP** (quad = FALSE): * Build covariance \(\;C = K_xx + ^2_n I\) via cov_generator. * Compute Cholesky factor \(L L^T = C\). * Log-determinant: \((C) = 2(diag(L))\). * Precision \(Q = C^-1 = chol2inv(L)\). * Negative log-likelihood: \[ 12\,y^T Q\,y \;-\; (Q) \;-\; [LogNormal(length\_scale prior\_l)]. \]

    **GP with quadratic mean** (quad = TRUE): * Construct design matrix \(X = [1,\,x,\,unique(x x)]\). * Build \(C = K_xx + ^2_n I\) and its precision \(Q\). * Form marginal precision \(S = X^T Q X\) and invert via Cholesky. * Compute two quadratic terms: \(12\,y^T Q\,y\) and \(12\,y^T Q X S^-1 X^T Q\,y\). * Combine with log-determinants of \(Q\) and \(S^-1\) and the log-prior to yield the final negative log-likelihood.

    Examples

    # Zero-mean SE kernel likelihood
x <- matrix(seq(0,1,length.out=5), ncol=1)
y <- sin(2*pi*x)
like0 <- compute_like(length_scale = 0.2,
                      x = x, y = y,
                      signal_var = 1,
                      noise_var  = 1e-3,
                      D = 1,
                      prior_l_mean = 0,
                      prior_l_sd   = 1,
                      quad = FALSE,
                      nu   = Inf)
#> Error in compute_like(length_scale = 0.2, x = x, y = y, signal_var = 1,     noise_var = 0.001, D = 1, prior_l_mean = 0, prior_l_sd = 1,     quad = FALSE, nu = Inf): unused arguments (prior_l_mean = 0, prior_l_sd = 1)

# GP with quadratic mean
like2 <- compute_like(length_scale = 0.3,
                      x = x, y = y,
                      signal_var = 1,
                      noise_var  = 1e-3,
                      D = 1,
                      prior_l_mean = 0,
                      prior_l_sd   = 1,
                      quad = TRUE,
                      nu   = Inf)
#> Error in compute_like(length_scale = 0.3, x = x, y = y, signal_var = 1,     noise_var = 0.001, D = 1, prior_l_mean = 0, prior_l_sd = 1,     quad = TRUE, nu = Inf): unused arguments (prior_l_mean = 0, prior_l_sd = 1)
